lead: everyone who describes the marriage describes one person taking on another. it is said kindly. the terms the two of you set were even, agreed in one afternoon, by two people with the same amount to lose.
sun: seen from across a room, the pair of you prices out as a large amount of one person and an ordinary amount of another, and an even agreement between those two is not visible from any seat in the place. so the keeping is put down to you: twenty years of showing up, logged as something you could afford, and the part where you were held to something appears in nobody's version.
moon: you chose it, on a day you can still name, knowing what it would ask. choosing does not show; capacity shows. so a thing renewed by decision every year gets credited to the size instead — of course it holds, look at it — and the correction is the one sentence neither of you has said out loud to anyone in all that time.
pull: the two of you agreed to the same thing on the same afternoon. every account since has one of you being carried, both families tell it that way, and it has never been correctable.
tension: at every gathering someone tells them they landed well, warmly, in your hearing, and they laugh and agree because disagreeing takes a speech. what the arrangement asks of them is not visible at this distance — the years they carried it, the thing they gave up in the second decade, the nights it was them holding the whole of it. a marriage cannot be audited from the door, and the door is where everyone has stood.
cost: nobody worries about the two of you, which is why the people who ring at one in the morning about their own arrangement ring you. that traffic runs one direction. a bond that reads sound is not a bond anybody checks, so the year it was in trouble the pair of you got through it unassisted, and nobody has since found out there was a year.

lead: the date beside your name is the earliest on the board and anyone can read it off the wall. it is the one thing about you that is not an impression, and it records only that you turned up first.
sun: the board gives everyone the same rights in the same order, and yours come first. taking them is where the trouble is. somebody smaller picking the good run is a man using his date; you doing it is a large thing helping itself, visible from the yard, discussed by people who would have done the same. so the rights you hold on paper get used about half as often as they are owed.
moon: seniority arrived by subtraction — two ahead of you retired, one died, and on an ordinary tuesday the top of the list was you, with nothing above it. that removes the only people who could have corrected the reading: the ones who knew you at nineteen, who watched you learn it, who would have said so. the last of them left six years ago.
pull: one line of the record is checkable and the rest of you is an impression. the impression is what gets obeyed. the line is the part you did nothing to earn except last.
tension: you took the week everybody wants in your second year at the top, which the board says is yours and always was, and it went round the yard as a change in you. men who have taken the same week for years read it out of the same column and nobody notices them. the reading does not adjust for paperwork. so a right that is written down and dated still lands as appetite when you are the one exercising it.
cost: people two grades down bring you things that ought to go to a manager, and the things get settled, because a post with nothing above it and somebody that size on top of it reads as where matters end. the settling runs on the size. the same words, with the same date behind them, out of the mouth of whoever is second on that board, would go nowhere.

lead: he taught you for six years and you took his method to the bottom of itself at forty, and what you found there was ordinary, and the saying of it went out at a width you do not set.
sun: it was said once, at a dinner, to four people. it did not stay at that dinner — it left the room already scaled to whoever said it, and inside a year it was the settled view of a man who had taught for thirty years. you did not repeat it. nothing needed repeating. what you had was a doubt; what arrived at his door was a judgement with weight behind it.
moon: the question was never rhetorical. you wanted to know what the method stood on, and finding out meant lifting it, and lifting it is how a thing dies. your own six years came out of that ground. so what you hold now of where you came from includes the afternoon you established there was less under it than anyone had been told.
pull: you went to the bottom of the thing you came out of, the report went out at your size, and no version of that finding stayed between you and him.
tension: his people say you cleared the ground above yourself, and it is not answerable, because from where they sit the sequence is a big one going under a small one and coming up with the space he was occupying. being right does not help. right at your scale looks like a thing done for room, and the man is seventy-one, and nobody has since decided whether the method worked.
cost: going under the thing that made you is not something most people manage, and you did it to the method you owe your hands to, and said what was there. no one is left now whose student you could be. the men who taught alongside him answer your calls carefully, and the finding stands, unopposed, in a field that has stopped discussing him.

lead: a crowd is the one place a person is supposed to stop being a person. six hundred of you in the corner of a ground, and the photograph the next day is of you, in the middle of it.
sun: the stewards walk toward you. the club wrote to you after the trouble, and the letter opened as though it had reached an office. nothing here has a membership or officers, and nobody appointed anybody — six hundred people have a spokesman because one of them can be picked out from the far side of a stand, and the picking out was done years ago by people who have never spoken to you.
moon: belonging here has always come with a small distance in it, and everybody else stands where they stand without one. you sort them without meaning to: one season in, you know which of the new ones will still be travelling in three years and which are here for a winter. you are right about it. the ones you have written off can tell.
pull: the point of a crowd is that nobody in it is anybody. you have stood in one every other weekend since you were sixteen, and it has closed over everybody in there except you.
tension: the version that goes round is that you like it — that somebody quoted in a local paper after every incident has arranged to be. people who have travelled with you for fifteen years say it fondly. it is also the only explanation available, because the same face is in every photograph and nobody took a single one deliberately. the winter you missed half the season, what stuck was that you had got what you came for.
cost: twenty years of arriving early means you know which of them is in trouble at home before his own row does, and the corner runs better for it — a lift found, a ticket held. the sorting is not neutral, though. a view you keep to yourself about who is serious travels anyway, at your width, and two men stopped coming without anybody saying a word to them.
